title: Mary the Paralegal
cn: 第 19 集 · 助理律师玛丽
novel:
Barney brought a woman to a formal dinner and introduced her as a [[paralegal|paralegal]].

Ted did not [[assume|assume]] anything at first. Then Barney winked twice, and a stupid [[rumour|rumour]] took root in Ted's head. All evening he tried not to stare, [[muttering|mutter]] questions to Marshall behind his glass.

The dinner was an [[award|award]] night. Robin was a [[nominee|nominee]]. When her name was read out there was warm [[applause|applause]], and she walked to the [[podium|podium]] looking calm and proud.

Ted should have been happy. Instead he felt [[jealous|jealous]] of the man who had come as her [[escort|escort]], and quietly [[resented|resent]] the whole room.

He made one [[sarcastic|sarcastic]] joke too many. It landed like an [[insult|insult]]. Robin was [[offended|offend]].

"That was [[outrageous|outrageous]]," she said outside. "Do you hear yourself?"

He tried to [[clarify|clarify]] what he had meant, then realised the truth was worse than the [[misunderstanding|misunderstanding]]. His [[accusation|accusation]] had been [[spiteful|spiteful]], and he could not [[defend|defend]] it.

So he said one [[sincere|sincere]] sentence instead of ten clever ones.

Barney, meanwhile, got a [[punch|punch]] in the arm — and deserved it.

paralegal.en: a person who helps a lawyer but is not a lawyer

assume.en: to believe something is true without checking

rumour.en: a story people tell each other that may not be true

mutter.en: to speak quietly and unclearly, often when annoyed

award.en: a prize given for good work

nominee.en: a person chosen as one of the people who might win

applause.en: the sound of many people clapping

podium.en: the small raised stand a speaker stands on

jealous.en: unhappy because someone else has what you want

escort.en: a person who goes with someone to an event

resent.en: to feel angry about something you think is unfair

sarcastic.en: saying the opposite of what you mean, to hurt or joke

insult.en: a rude thing said to hurt someone

offend.en: to make someone feel upset or angry

clarify.en: to explain something so it becomes clear

misunderstanding.en: a mistake about what someone meant

accusation.en: a statement that someone did something bad

spiteful.en: wanting to hurt someone on purpose

defend.en: to say words that support or protect someone

sincere.en: honest, and really meaning what you say

punch.en: a hit with a closed hand
